source.title: Enhancing LMMSE Performance with Modest Complexity Increase via Neural Network Equalizers
source.authors: Vadim Rozenfeld; D. Raphaeli; Oded Bialer

record.file_problem: None; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study trains neural equalizers and discusses optimization difficulties, but it does not test the claim versions’ training classification error, teacher-student local minima, network depth, activation-matched initialization, learning-rate stability, or batch normalization conditions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports BER comparisons and states that randomly initialized equalizers mostly gain negligibly over LMMSE, while its proposed LMMSE-based initialization improves BER. These results concern symbol equalization and LLR matching, not the training classification-error behavior named by the claim versions. It also cites prior work on spurious minima; those cited results are not this study’s results.
record.test_reason: The study measures held-out equalization BER after training compact fully connected networks to match MAP-generated LLRs. It does not measure any version's specified training behavior. Its initialization comparison concerns final BER, without training speed, trainable depth, or signal and gradient propagation measurements for V4. The ReLU teacher-student local-minimum findings are cited rather than tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' conclusion: compact neural equalizers encounter optimization difficulties, and their LMMSE-based initialization and progressively extended architectures improve BER with modest computational overhead, including in turbo equalization. The authors attribute poor random-initialization performance to local minima, but the reported BER comparisons do not directly establish convergence to such minima.
record.recipe_differences: Trains compact fully connected neural equalizers to approximate MAP-generated symbol LLRs, using Adam and an LMMSE-based initialization; reports BER on ISI channels rather than classification training error on image benchmarks.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization choice changes the reported BER performance; the paper also varies channel, modulation, and uncoded versus turbo equalization conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: Randomly initialized 2-EqzNet models mostly provide negligible BER gains over LMMSE; the proposed initialization improves (8, 2)-EqzNet performance by approximately 3.5 dB on uncoded 2-PAM over hA.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LMMSE-based initialization and the associated training procedure can improve final BER performance of compact neural equalizers relative to random initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: The proposed equalizers outperform LMMSE on hA and, for 6-EqzNet on hB, nearly match MAP performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Compact neural equalizers can improve equalization BER over LMMSE with modest additional computational complexity.

record.problems: The relevant initialization comparisons are reported mainly through BER plots and qualitative text; no uncertainty estimates are stated. The reported task and metrics do not directly measure classification training error.

untested.parts: Training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels and size, stopping, and regularization conditions.
Spurious-minimum frequency in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and the effect of adding student neurons beyond teacher width.
Depth-dependent training degradation, identity shortcuts, and the specified initialization and normalization exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization preserving signals and gradients; training speed and trainable depth; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization and very deep convolutional networks.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, transient loss increases, curvature dynamics, edge-of-stability training, and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup's normalization-free training.

record.verdict_notes: All rows remain unlinked to V1–V6. BER is evaluated using separate test data; neither training loss trajectories nor direct local-minimum diagnostics are reported.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted or random labels; model size, stopping, and regularization conditions.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious-minimum frequency, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual network depth and training error; special initialization or normalization-free residual training.
Activation-matched initialization, signal or gradient propagation, trainable depth, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and 10,000-layer convolutional networks.
Learning rates above stability limits, loss and curvature dynamics, sharpness, and divergence.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup training without normalization.
